task: Task 2: mcp.rs server surfaces + anonymous allowlist + tools/list enrichment
summary: The implementation is secure for its scope. The anonymous allowlist enforcement is correct, no per-tenant or sensitive data leaks through the new discovery surfaces, and the URI/name input validation is structurally sound (stem matched against a compile-time static set, not the filesystem). Two low-severity findings and one forward-looking advisory for Task 4.

findings.title: Tool description contains internal implementation artifact
findings.description: The description for the `request_public_write_confirmation` tool reads: "Consumed by Task 4's handler; not user-facing — agent skills invoke it inline whenever they intend to issue a `mode='participate'` write with `visibility='public'`." The phrase 'Consumed by Task 4's handler' is an internal development artifact referencing the project's task numbering system. This is exposed anonymously via `tools/list`.
findings.impact: An anonymous MCP client can infer that the tool has no handler yet and that the project is following a numbered task structure. Not a secret, but it signals an incomplete implementation surface that an adversary could probe.
findings.recommendation: Remove the 'Consumed by Task 4's handler; not user-facing' fragment from the public-facing description before the v1 release. Replace with functional description only: e.g., 'Request a signed confirmation token required for public participate-mode writes. Call before sign_memory with mode=participate and visibility=public.'

findings.title: No explicit length cap on `name` / `uri` parameters in discovery handlers
findings.description: The `name` field in `prompts/get` and the `uri` field in `resources/read` are accepted from the JSON-RPC params without an explicit length check. On a failure path (`invalid_params`), the full received value is echoed back in `data.received`. The body is globally bounded by `MAX_PEEK_BODY = 1 MiB` in the OAuth middleware, so the maximum echo size is bounded, but there is no per-field cap.
findings.impact: A client could send a name/uri of up to ~1 MiB, causing the server to allocate, parse, and echo a large string in the JSON-RPC error response. This is a mild amplification vector (1:1 echo, no multiplication) bounded by the existing 1 MiB body cap. Not a DoS risk given existing rate limiting, but the pattern is not defense-in-depth.
findings.recommendation: Add a short length check before the lookup: e.g., `if name.len() > 128 { return Err(invalid_params("name", &Value::String(name.to_string()))); }`. Skill names are at most ~32 chars; URIs are at most ~64. A 256-byte cap per field eliminates the echo amplification while imposing zero ergonomic cost on legitimate clients.

findings.category: Defense in Depth — Forward Advisory for Task 4
findings.title: request_public_write_confirmation handler (Task 4) must re-verify JWT presence
findings.location: mcp/src/mcp.rs — future Task 4 handler dispatch arm
findings.description: The `request_public_write_confirmation` tool is listed in `tools/list` (anonymous-visible) and correctly NOT placed in `ALLOWLIST_METHODS`. The OAuth middleware gate enforces JWT requirement on `tools/call` today — any anonymous `tools/call` for this tool gets a 401 before reaching the dispatcher. However, per the threat model in tech-spec Decision 5b, the handler itself must independently verify that `Claims` is `Some` (i.e., a valid JWT is present) and derive `owner_pubkey` exclusively from `claims.sub`, never from client-supplied parameters. This is defense-in-depth against future middleware refactoring that might inadvertently allowlist `tools/call`.
findings.impact: If Task 4's handler is written without an explicit `Claims` check and a future change accidentally allowlists `tools/call`, an anonymous caller could invoke the ceremony gate without authentication, bypassing the ownership binding in the HMAC tuple (tech-spec Decision 5b: 'owner_pubkey is derived server-side from claims.sub — never client-supplied').
findings.recommendation: Task 4 must include: (1) An explicit `match claims { Some(c) => c, None => return Err(JsonRpcError::simple(-32001, "unauthorized")) }` guard at handler entry, before any HMAC computation. (2) A dedicated integration test case: call `request_public_write_confirmation` without Bearer token → assert HTTP 401 (middleware) AND separately assert the handler returns -32001 if somehow called with Claims=None (defense-in-depth unit test).

pass_checks.check: Anonymous allowlist enforcement — no non-allowlisted method reachable anonymously
pass_checks.detail: ALLOWLIST_METHODS now contains exactly: [initialize, tools/list, ping, prompts/list, prompts/get, resources/list, resources/read]. The `notifications/*` prefix passthrough is safe: arbitrary `notifications/X` methods hit the dispatcher's catch-all `_ => Err(unknown method)` arm and return -32603 with no data access. The literal `notifications/initialized` arm returns `{}`. No tool execution path is reachable without a valid JWT.

pass_checks.check: No path traversal in resource URI handling
pass_checks.detail: resources_read_payload() strips the RESOURCE_URI_PREFIX ('mnemonik://skills/') and '.md' suffix, then does a linear scan against ALL_SKILLS (a compile-time static slice). No filesystem call is made anywhere in the new handlers. An attacker cannot supply '../../../etc/passwd' or similar — the stem would not match any registered skill name and returns -32602.

pass_checks.check: No owner_pubkey / signer_pubkey / JWT sub leakage in anonymous responses
pass_checks.detail: The four new dispatcher arms (prompts/list, prompts/get, resources/list, resources/read) call functions that accept only (&Value) or no parameters. None reference owner_pubkey, jwt_sub, or state.keypair. The initialize response now includes embedder.{model_id, model_version, dim} — these are public model identity fields, not user credentials. For anonymous requests, owner_pubkey falls back to state.keypair (server's own Ed25519 pubkey) but this value is not surfaced in any new response field.

pass_checks.check: No embeddings or canonical CBOR bytes returned anonymously
pass_checks.detail: prompts/* and resources/* return only skill manifest markdown (mcp/assets/skills/*.md content) — public documentation. No search results, embedding vectors, attestation records, or CBOR bytes are reachable on these paths.

pass_checks.check: URI echo in success path is bounded to valid canonical URIs only
pass_checks.detail: In resources_read_payload(), the user-supplied `uri` is echoed in the success response contents[0].uri ONLY after passing both prefix/suffix validation AND stem lookup against ALL_SKILLS. Any URI that reaches the echo point is structurally 'mnemonik://skills/<valid_skill_name>.md' — the effective value space is at most 7 strings.

pass_checks.check: request_public_write_confirmation tools/call blocked for anonymous callers
pass_checks.detail: tools/call is not in ALLOWLIST_METHODS. Anonymous POST to /mcp with method=tools/call receives HTTP 401 from bearer_auth_middleware before the dispatcher is invoked. The tool definition in tools/list (anonymous-visible) exposes only name + inputSchema — no sensitive server data.

pass_checks.check: No log injection via user-supplied name/uri values
pass_checks.detail: Grepped new handler functions for tracing/log macro calls. None of the new prompts_get_payload(), resources_read_payload(), prompts_list_payload(), resources_list_payload(), enrich_tool_description(), or skill_for_tool() functions emit log lines containing user-supplied values.

pass_checks.check: Skill manifest content — no secrets baked into binary
pass_checks.detail: Spot-checked mcp/assets/skills/attest.md and init.md. Content is purely user-facing behavioral guidance. No API keys, private keys, internal service URLs, or credentials are present in the manifests.
